frontier_act_119.text: This week, America's leading AI companies signed the White House Accord, an important step toward ensuring that the most advanced AI systems are developed responsibly. The Accord embraces several principles at the heart of our bipartisan FRONTIER Act: robust internal risk management, strong corporate governance, and independent third-party evaluation.

deepseek.reason: The speaker calls the FRONTIER Act 'our bipartisan' bill and highlights its core principles.
deepseek.confidence_reason: Self-identification as a sponsor of the named bill.

frontier_act_119.text:
Today, the NSA warned organizations to patch two critical security flaws in PHP or take their systems offline. PHP is the software behind roughly 7 in 10 websites, from small business storefronts to town, school and government portals.
 
Attackers began exploiting these flaws before the fix was released, and what’s even more concerning is that many sites run versions too old to receive the update at all.
 
This is the new reality of cybersecurity in the age of AI. Advanced AI systems can now uncover serious vulnerabilities in the code that underpins the internet. That capability can strengthen our defenses, but it can just as easily be turned against us.
 
Congress is running out of time to act.
 
We should start now with the FRONTIER Act, which would place serious, durable guardrails on the most powerful AI systems. We should pair it with a liability regime like my CLAIM Act that compels companies to prioritize safety and gives those who are harmed a path to recourse. And we must make the investments in cyber defense that this moment urgently demands.

deepseek.reason: The speaker says Congress should start now with the FRONTIER Act.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly calls for starting now with the FRONTIER Act.

frontier_act_119.text:
Powerful AI models are breaking out of their own labs, onto the internet, and hacking into other companies. 

Don’t take it from me. Top AI researchers and developers are resigning and warning that these companies are only worried about racing to the top and developing the most powerful models as fast as possible. 

One thing is clear: We can't rely on AI companies to police themselves.

The FRONTIER Act puts real guardrails in place. It has bipartisan support. We can get it done.

https://t.co/rNgL1cfy4v

deepseek.reason: The speaker says the FRONTIER Act puts real guardrails in place and can get done.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement explicitly promotes the FRONTIER Act as real guardrails.

It's past time for Congress to get off the sidelines and do its job. We can start with my bipartisan FRONTIER Act.

To make matters worse, there’s no federal law that requires the disclosure of these breaches whatsoever.

Congress has a duty to protect Americans from the catastrophic risks of advanced AI, including potential cyberattacks, development of biological threats, or large-scale harm. When the House returns, we should take up the bipartisan FRONTIER Act.

That's what my bipartisan FRONTIER Act fixes.

That’s why I introduced the bipartisan FRONTIER Act.

https://t.co/iTJghlwlAm

deepseek.reason: The speaker says she introduced the bipartisan FRONTIER Act.

frontier_act_119.text:
The White House has created a framework that shapes access to the most advanced AI models. It’s disappointing that they have chosen to block its public release.

Clearly some of this work touches real security concerns, but we should all be worried about the prospect of our national approach living behind a secretive wall — whether at DHS, the intelligence community or another agency. AI governance belongs in a civilian agency, where it can be seen and questioned, not buried inside the national security apparatus. Secrecy by default doesn’t make us safer.

The framework should be public so everyone, from the companies to the safety watchdogs to the American people, knows the rule book and can hold the referees accountable, and Congress should lead in setting those rules. That’s what my bipartisan FRONTIER Act will deliver.

deepseek.reason: The speaker says her bipartisan FRONTIER Act will deliver public AI rules.

Voluntary transparency isn't enough.

My bipartisan FRONTIER Act establishes commonsense guardrails for AI. When Congress returns, we need hearings, oversight and legislative action before it’s too late.

https://t.co/kKd2lTXJ4R
